WITH upd AS (UPDATE salon.conversations SET stage = 'new', last_intent = '' WHERE id = $1 AND stage = 'handoff' AND salon.at_ts(last_updated) = $2 AND last_updated <= to_timestamp($4::double precision) + interval '1 second' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM salon.processed_messages WHERE message_id = $3) RETURNING id, salon.at_ts(created_at) AS "createdTime", jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object('sender_key', NULLIF(sender_key, ''), 'stage', NULLIF(stage, ''), 'slot_service', NULLIF(slot_service, ''), 'slot_date', NULLIF(slot_date, ''), 'slot_time', NULLIF(slot_time, ''), 'last_updated', salon.at_ts(last_updated), 'turn_count', turn_count, 'last_intent', NULLIF(last_intent, ''), 'recent_messages', NULLIF(recent_messages, ''), 'gcal_event_id', NULLIF(gcal_event_id, ''), 'cancel_target_id', NULLIF(cancel_target_id, ''), 'confirm_turn', NULLIF(confirm_turn, ''), 'computed_reply', NULLIF(computed_reply, ''), 'last_alert_class', NULLIF(last_alert_class, ''), 'last_alert_at', salon.at_ts(last_alert_at), 'sender_masked', NULLIF(sender_masked, ''))) AS fields), mark AS (INSERT INTO salon.processed_messages (message_id, sender_key, channel) SELECT $3, 'owner:dashboard', 'owner' FROM upd ON CONFLICT (message_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING 1) SELECT * FROM upd UNION ALL SELECT NULL::text AS id, NULL::text AS "createdTime", jsonb_build_object('released', false, 'conflict', CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM salon.processed_messages WHERE message_id = $3) THEN 'replay' ELSE 'state_changed' END) AS fields WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM upd)

## Two layers, and they answer DIFFERENT questions
Cloudflare Access Service Auth (in front, `/webhook/owner-*`) answers **which machine**. The HMAC here answers **which request**. Both are required: if the service token ever leaks, the signature is the only thing left standing.

Raw body ON — the signature is over the exact bytes the dashboard sent.

## The allow-list is the security model
Exactly ONE verb: `release_handoff`. `prompt-injection.md` — there is no other write action, so there is nothing for a compromise to escalate into. This is also why CRT #11 is auditable: the surface is one verb.

Mirrors `OWNER_ACTIONS` in `lib/ownerAction.ts`. Two places, on purpose.

## A signature does not say WHICH conversation
All required, or nothing is written: the record exists (a lookup ERROR answers 503, not 404) · `stage === 'handoff'` · touched within 30 days and not in the future · and, in the release statement itself, the row still carries the version token this request read and was not touched after the signed `ts` (+1 s), and no marker exists for this message id. Otherwise 404 (missing) / 409 (not locked or changed since it was read).

Without this, one valid signature unlocks ARBITRARY conversations — the same hole the endpoint exists to close, just moved inside the fence.

## Replay: what actually holds (7-2 Tur 2 O1, R2b OA-1)
`Release Handoff Lock` is ONE statement. It releases only if no marker exists for this message id, the row is still the handoff `Validate Release Target` read (`stage='handoff'` and the same `last_updated`), and that handoff was written no later than the signed request's `ts` (+1 s). It writes the marker ONLY when that UPDATE released a row, so a marker means "this request released". Otherwise one sentinel row (`released:false`, `conflict: replay` when the marker existed at statement start, else `state_changed`) and nothing is written. A delayed duplicate cannot release a NEWER handoff, and a refused request leaves no marker. `Check Owner Replay` stays as the fast path for a sequential replay.

## Write-then-verify
Airtable and the engine share no transaction. A 200 is not a confirmed write — `booking-integrity.md` requires the re-read on every mutation path.

`stage` AND `last_intent` TOGETHER: two escalation ladders read `last_intent`, so clearing only `stage` leaves the conversation half-armed and it re-locks on the next uncertain turn.

## Failure is VISIBLE
A release that did not happen must never look like one that did. Separate alert class, separate branch, 502 to the caller.

⚠ This leaf is TERMINAL — no alert about a failed alert (infinite loop).
